newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC finance chiefs support private sector's call.
newsitem.headline: APEC finance chiefs support private sector's call.

text.p: Asia Pacific finance ministers have expressed support for measures urged by private financiers to increase fund flows in the region, Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Saturday..
But he said they stopped short of setting timetables for implementing the moves..

"The consensus is that those are good ideas ... We are supportive of the thrusts and directions of the group," de Ocampo, who is chairing the fourth APEC (Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation) finance ministers' meeting, told reporters after meeting with the APEC Financiers Group..
The group, made up of top investment bankers and fund managers, met on Friday to firm up the recommendations passed on to the ministers on Saturday.

The group called for concrete steps to promote financial market development, such as cross listing of securities on various stock markets and standardisation of accounting principles that companies must follow.
However, the finance ministers did not set specific timetables for implementing the recommendations, de Campo said.

"There's a consensus that the idea of opening up, liberalisation, private sector participation is the way to go. Nobody is forcing anybody to do it along any particular timing. Everybody has his own timing and it is recognised by everybody," he added..

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and the United States.
